title: Asymmetric-loss abstention and claim-specific reopening board
hypothesis: A claim-specific decision board can represent asymmetric loss and force abstention when required loss weights, evidence, authority, or independent review are absent, without letting strong local engineering evidence compensate for a missing external gate.
null_or_failure: Loss weights are invented by the technical owner, a global score overrides a veto, defer is relabeled pass, reopening occurs without new qualifying evidence, negatives shrink, one pillar compensates for another, or a local board becomes Stage 20 readiness.
test_falsifier_or_gate: Mutate loss ownership, evidence class, veto state, disposition, negative count, reopening evidence, authority, independent reviewer, and pillar status; require abstention or defer whenever a qualifying prerequisite is absent and retain NOT_READY_FOR_STAGE_20.
rollback_or_recovery: Restore the claim-specific defer state, retain the failed promotion vector, preserve every veto and negative, and reopen only after new qualifying empirical, production, legal, cultural, accessibility, security, or independent evidence is supplied by the competent source.
boundary: The abstention board has missing external loss ownership and qualifying evidence; Stage 20 readiness remains false.
